LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 12 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: What can you learn from poems and songs? 2. Which poems and songs do you know? 3. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words while reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. create mental images from events, characters and places in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. infer information and meaning of words from context,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate events and characters in the reading text to personal experiences.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. create mental images from events, characters and places in a text,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. infer information and meaning of words from context,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension,

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. relate events and characters in the reading text to personal experiences.

   Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a video on environmental pollution and answer questions,

2. read a poem or song and role play the events, experiences or characters in the text,

3. answer factual and inferential questions on the poem and song they read,

4. visualise events, characters or places mentioned in a text,

5. draw visuals to summarise information from a text,

6. role play events or characters in the poem collaboratively with peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a video on environmental pollution and answer questions,
2. read a poem or song and role play the events, experiences or characters in the text,
3. answer factual and inferential questions on the poem and song they read,
4. visualise events, characters or places mentioned in a text,
5. draw visuals to summarise information from a text,
6. role play events or characters in the poem collaboratively with peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration is enhanced as the learner role plays events or characters in the poem collaboratively with peers.

• Digital Literacy is developed as the learner watches a video on a poem about environmental pollution.

Values:
Responsibility is promoted when learners read poems/listen to songs and answer questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education is enhanced as the learner interacts with content on environmental pollution.

Life Skills Education – Communication skills are enhanced as the learner recites poems and sing songs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the content of songs and poems to what is learnt in Creative Arts.

The learner applies the content of Environmental Pollution to a concept learnt in Science and Technology.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. create mental images from events, characters and places in a text,
2. infer information and meaning of words from context,
3. answer factual and inferential questions correctly for comprehension,
4. relate events and characters in the reading text to personal experiences.

Remember the key question: What can you learn from poems and songs? 2. Which poems and songs do you know? 3. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words while reading?
